docRequirement: `best-practices.md:469` binds the non-interactive run's session lifecycle: "The run still creates a resumable session unless you pass `--no-session-persistence`." Persistence is the DEFAULT and discarding is the opt-in, through a flag spelled exactly `--no-session-persistence`; `cli-reference.md:103` fixes its semantics — "Disable session persistence so sessions are not saved to disk and cannot be resumed. Print mode only. The `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` environment variable does the same in any mode" — i.e. never-written, not written-then-removed.
current: The fork's `-p` analogue is `nessy-general-agent run` (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:616-618` says so in a comment; `:782` spawns the server with `printMode: true` → `PRINT_MODE_ENV_VAR` from `packages/shared/src/config/print-background-wait.ts:47`). Its default is the inverse. `cleanup()` at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:787-793` runs `await client.invoke('sessions:delete', sessionId)` whenever `!args.noCleanup`, and it runs on every exit path: success `:853`, error `:858`, SIGINT/SIGTERM `:800` (so an interrupted run is destroyed too). `noCleanup` is fed only by `--no-cleanup` (declared `:37`, defaulted `false` at `:66`, parsed `:113-114`), so persistence is the opt-in — help text `:2052` "--no-cleanup        Keep session after completion", `docs/cli.md:168` "`--no-cleanup` | `false` | Skip session deletion on exit", `docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:177` "Deletes the session and stops the server — unless `--no-cleanup` is set" and `:188`, ru mirror `docs-site/content/ru/reference/cli.md:168,179`. The delete is a hard durable removal, not a soft one: `SessionManager.deleteSession` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:14920`) fences the persistence queue and then `if (this.sessionStore.delete(sessionKey) === false) throw new Error('session-storage-delete-failed')` at `:14950-14952`, emitting `session_deleted` at `:15017`. The session lived in the user's REAL store first: `apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:62-71` passes the parent env through with no `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` or `mkdtemp` override, and `docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:177` states the spawned server shares `CONFIG_DIR` with the desktop app. `--no-session-persistence` does not exist: `grep -ran 'no-session-persistence|noSessionPersistence|PROMPT_HISTORY' apps/cli apps/electron/src packages/*/src docs/*.md` returns nothing (NUL-safe; the only `sessionPersistence` hits are the unrelated `SessionPersistenceQueue` in `apps/electron/dist/main.cjs`). Because parseArgs' default branch pushes any unrecognised dash-argument into `rest` (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:160-165`) and `cmdRun` builds the prompt from `rest` via `readPrompt(args.rest, args.rest)` (`:766`, joined at `:424`), passing the documented flag concatenates the literal string `--no-session-persistence` into the prompt sent to the model. The run also never prints the session id in text mode (`sessionId` is set at `:846` and only leaks inside raw event JSON under `--output-format stream-json`, `:470`), and `send`/`sessions` require `--url` (`:2172-2175`), so even a `--no-cleanup` run leaves a session the CLI cannot name. The mechanism the doc actually describes already exists internally and is unused by the CLI: `ephemeral` ("In-memory only; never writes the session record or metadata to disk") is on the wire DTO at `packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:270-274`, on the store options at `packages/shared/src/sessions/store-v2.ts:60-62`, threaded through `SessionManager.createSession` at `:9190` and `:9289`, and covered by `packages/server-core/src/sessions/ephemeral-session.test.ts`; the CLI's `sessions:create` call at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:841-845` passes only `permissionMode`, `enabledSourceSlugs` and `projectHandleId`.
divergence: Two deltas, and the first is polarity, not naming. (1) Inverted default: with no flags, upstream keeps a resumable session and we hard-delete it; the same command produces opposite outcomes. (2) The opt-in is inverted with it and spelled differently — ours is `--no-cleanup` meaning "keep", the doc's is `--no-session-persistence` meaning "discard" — and the discard MECHANISM differs too: the doc says such sessions "are not saved to disk" (never written, which is exactly our existing `ephemeral: true`), whereas we write the record and then remove it durably. Missing alongside: the `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` env equivalent that upstream honours "in any mode". Not covered by the row but worth stating so nobody thinks the flag alone closes it: `run` never prints the session id, so a kept session has no user-visible handle.

blastRadius: This crosses a PERSISTENCE boundary — a repo risk trigger — in the direction of writing more, not less: today `run` leaves nothing behind, and after the fix every headless run leaves a durable session record in the shared `CONFIG_DIR` that the desktop app also reads (`docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:177`; `apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:62-71` inherits the parent env, so CI runs land in `~/.nessy-agent` unless `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` is set). Whatever bounds that growth is `packages/shared/src/sessions/retention-sweep.ts` (a `deleteSession` caller per codegraph) — check its policy applies to headless-created sessions before shipping. It does NOT cross a wire/schema boundary: `ephemeral` is already on `CreateSessionOptions` (`packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:274`, `packages/shared/src/sessions/store-v2.ts:60-62`) and already honoured server-side (`SessionManager.ts:9190`, `:9289`, and the ~20 `managed.ephemeral` guards from `:3079` to `:18590`). Readers of the CLI flag: `apps/cli/src/index.ts` only (`noCleanup` appears at `:37`, `:66`, `:114`, `:181`, `:788` and nowhere else in `apps`/`packages`). Tests touched: `apps/cli/src/commands.test.ts:206-214`, `apps/cli/src/run.test.ts:223-230`. The optional server-side env force at `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:285-291` sits on the single `sessions:create` channel but `SessionManager.createSession` has 18 callers (`packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts`, internal branch/child paths) — an env-forced `ephemeral` would reach branch and child-session creation too, so scope the check to the RPC handler rather than the method unless that is deliberate. `sessions:delete` itself keeps its other callers (`cmdSessionDelete`, `apps/cli/src/index.ts:414`; desktop UI) untouched.
userImpact: Two observable failures today. (1) A headless run's session is destroyed: after `nessy-general-agent run "…"` exits, the session is absent from the Nessy Desktop sidebar, `sessions` cannot list it and `send <id>` cannot continue it, and the removal is a hard durable-storage delete (`SessionManager.ts:14950-14952`), so the transcript is unrecoverable — including on Ctrl+C, which destroys the partial run (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:800`). Anyone porting a Claude Code CI recipe that inspects or resumes a `-p` run afterwards loses the data silently, with exit code 0. (2) Worse and immediately visible: passing the documented flag poisons the prompt. `nessy-general-agent run --no-session-persistence "audit this repo"` does not error on the unknown flag — `:160-165` pushes it into `rest` and `:766`/`:424` join `rest` into the prompt, so the model receives "--no-session-persistence audit this repo" and the session is deleted anyway. The user sees a run that answered a slightly wrong question and left nothing behind. Latent third: even `--no-cleanup` today gives no usable handle, because a text-mode run never prints the session id.
